biological_interpretation: SIN3A scaffold loss has a specific neuronal output that is not a generic REST, NuRD, HDAC, or MYC-family phenocopy despite shared repressor-complex annotations.
caveats: Perturbed-cell counts are modest and the target transcript was increased, not depleted, so transcript shift should not be used as a direct allelic loss readout.
Rest expression or guide activity was not independently measured here, so the absence of a Rest signature could be caused by weak perturbation, low Rest expression, or compensation.
The target gene panel is selective, all statistics are transcriptomic, and weak Rest RNA engagement limits directionality.
The correlations are modest in absolute value and are restricted-signature comparisons across genes, not biochemical evidence in the assayed cells.

Exact log2 fold changes, scores, p-values, and FDRs in exact_de_rows were re-read from the Wilcoxon Parquet; the graph and cluster summaries were used only to nominate the target/readout combinations.

prior_expectation.summary: References were retained only when they were linked to one of the resolved source findings.

finding_summaries.summary: Sin3a targeting generated a strongly cell-type-skewed response, with the majority of FDR signals in thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic neurons, midbrain glutamatergic neurons, Pvalb GABA neurons, and smaller midbrain/cerebral-nuclei GABA compartments.
finding_summaries.why_it_matters: Human SIN3A dosage disorders and mouse Sin3a studies are usually framed through cortical and hippocampal development; this dataset points to discrete subcortical excitatory and inhibitory populations as high-liability contexts for the acute transcriptional response.

finding_summaries.summary: Phf21a is not a simple Rest phenocopy in this neuronal atlas.
finding_summaries.why_it_matters: Although BHC/CoREST can be recruited by REST, Rest targeting produced no FDR-significant signature and did not induce Rreb1; the Phf21a effect is therefore likely routed through a REST-independent or REST-buffered context in these brain cells.

finding_summaries.summary: Selected REST/NRSE target genes were not derepressed after Rest targeting.
finding_summaries.why_it_matters: The result refines canonical REST biology by showing that the assayed mouse-brain populations did not enter the target-gene program seen in stem, non-neuronal, or stress contexts.

finding_summaries.summary: Max, but not Myc or Mycn, was a reproducible positive Sin3a signature neighbor in the major responder cell types.
finding_summaries.why_it_matters: SIN3A is known to be recruited by MXD/MAX-family repressors; the Max-specific convergence suggests that, in these neurons, removing Max resembles disrupting a SIN3A-linked repressor program more than perturbing Myc-family activators.

resolved_evidence.description: On-target RNA abundance did not show measurable differential expression after Rest targeting.

resolved_evidence.description: Selected curated or literature-linked REST target genes did not show a coherent FDR-supported derepression pattern.

resolved_evidence.description: Direct signature comparison between Sin3a and Myc/Max-family perturbations.
resolved_evidence.statistics: Pearson correlations between whole-transcriptome Wilcoxon-score signatures for Max and Sin3a were positive in the six strongest Sin3a responder contexts: r=0.233, rank 1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; r=0.158, rank 6 in 155 MB Glut; r=0.117, rank 7 in 052 Pvalb Gaba; r=0.121, rank 4 in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA; r=0.156, rank 7 in 191 MB P MY GABA; and r=0.046, rank 71 in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut. In the same six cell types, Myc had |r|<=0.023 and Mycn had |r|<=0.053.
